title: Lock In for 30 Minutes
short: Pick one thing, like tonight's homework or the song you're learning, and work only on that until the timer ends.
proof: What you worked on, after the timer.

title: Work on Your Top To-Do for 30 Minutes
short: Pick what matters most today, like studying for tomorrow's test or a paper due this week, and work on it.
proof: What you worked on, after the timer.

title: Finish One Thing You've Been Avoiding
short: Pick one task you keep putting off, like an email you owe, a form to fill out, or a pile of laundry, and finish it.
proof: The finished result. Cover anything private.

title: List 3 Things You Need to Do Tomorrow
short: Write down the three things that matter most tomorrow, like a quiz to study for or a form to turn in.
proof: Your written list of three.

title: Work With Your Phone Away for 30 Minutes
short: Start the timer, put your phone in a drawer or another room, and work on homework or another task until it ends.
proof: What you worked on, after the timer.

title: Finish Something You Left Half Done
short: Pick something you started but didn't finish, like a half-done worksheet or a drawer you were sorting, and finish it.
proof: The finished result. Cover anything private.

title: Study One Subject for 30 Minutes
short: Go over your notes, redo a few homework problems, or read the next chapter until the timer ends.
proof: A photo of your notes or the work in front of you. After the timer.

title: Test Yourself Without Looking at Your Notes
short: Close your notes and answer a few review questions from the end of a chapter or a study guide, then check them.
proof: Your answers, written from memory.

title: Complete 10 Practice Problems
short: Do ten practice problems for one class, like math problems from your textbook or questions from an old quiz.
proof: Your worked problems.

title: Write Everything You Remember About One Topic
short: Without opening your notes, fill a page with everything you remember about one topic, like the water cycle.
proof: What you wrote from memory.

title: Finish One Assignment
short: Finish one assignment so it's ready to turn in, like a worksheet, a lab write-up, or a discussion post.
proof: The finished assignment or its submitted screen. Hide your name and any grades.

title: Start an Assignment Before It's Urgent
short: Start an assignment that isn't due for a few days, like outlining an essay or reading the first chapter of a book.
proof: What you started, after the timer.

title: Turn Today's Notes Into 10 Questions
short: Read over today's notes from one class and write ten questions a test could ask about them.
proof: Your ten questions.

title: Test Yourself on Flashcards for 20 Minutes
short: Go through your flashcards, like vocab words or formulas, saying each answer before you flip the card.
proof: Your flashcards, after the timer.

title: Explain One Hard Topic in Your Own Words
short: Without your notes, write how you'd explain one hard topic to a friend, like solving for x or how photosynthesis works.
proof: Your explanation, written from memory.

title: Spend 30 Minutes on Your Hardest Class
short: Work on the class that's hardest for you, like redoing quiz questions you missed or rereading a confusing lesson.
proof: A photo of your notes or the work in front of you. After the timer.

title: Create Your Study Plan for the Week
short: Write what you'll study each day this week, like Monday for the history quiz and Wednesday for the essay.
proof: Your written plan.

title: Work on a School Project for 30 Minutes
short: Pick a school project that isn't due today, like a poster, a slideshow, or a research paper, and do the next part.
proof: Your project work, after the timer.

title: Review a Topic You Learned Earlier This Week
short: Go back to your notes from a class two or three days ago and quiz yourself on them until the timer ends.
proof: Your review, after the timer.

title: Complete Your Workout
short: Do the whole workout you planned for today, like a team practice, drills for your sport, or a dance routine.
proof: A photo of where you trained: the gym, your equipment, mat or shoes. Not your body.

title: Walk for 30 Minutes
short: Take a 30-minute walk, like laps around your block, the long way home, or a loop at a park.
proof: Where you walked, after the timer. Not your face.

title: Do 20 Minutes of Cardio
short: Do something that keeps you breathing hard for 20 minutes, like jumping rope, dancing, or running stairs.
proof: Where you did it, after the timer. Not your body.

title: Complete a 30-Minute At-Home Workout
short: Do a 30-minute workout at home with what you have, like push-ups, squats, and planks, or a workout video.
proof: Your workout space or equipment, after the timer. Not your body.

title: Get Outside and Move for 20 Minutes
short: Spend 20 minutes moving outside, like shooting hoops, skateboarding, or kicking a ball around.
proof: Where you were, after the timer. Not your face.

title: Complete Your Planned Strength Workout
short: Do every set of the strength workout you planned for today, like lifting weights at a gym or pull-ups at a park.
proof: A photo of where you trained: the gym, your equipment, mat or shoes. Not your body.

title: Do Your Planned Cardio Today
short: Do the cardio you planned for today, like a run, a bike ride, or a swim, and keep going until the timer ends.
proof: Where you did it, after the timer. Not your body.

title: Track Everything You Spend Today
short: Write down everything you spent today, even small things like a snack, a bus fare, or an in-app purchase.
proof: Your written list of what you spent. Written, never a bank or card screen.

title: Add Up What You Spent This Past Week
short: Sort the last seven days of purchases into groups, like food, clothes, and games, and add up each one.
proof: Your notes or a summary by category. Written, never a bank or card screen.

title: Make a Spending Plan for This Week
short: Write how you'll split the money you have, like allowance, gift money, or pay, between food, fun, and saving this week.
proof: Your written plan. Written, never a bank or card screen.

title: Decide If One Subscription Is Worth It
short: Pick one thing you pay for every month, like a music app or a game pass, and decide whether to keep it.
proof: A written note of the charge and what you decided. No account screenshots.

title: Set One Savings Goal and Deadline
short: Pick something you want to save for, like new shoes or a concert ticket, and write how much you need and by when.
proof: Your written goal, amount and deadline.

title: Improve One Resume Bullet
short: Rewrite one resume line to say what you did and the result, like money raised at a bake sale or customers you helped.
proof: The rewritten bullet. Hide anything personal.

title: Apply to One Job or Internship
short: Fill out and submit one application, like a part-time job at a store, a summer internship, or a scholarship.
proof: The submitted screen or confirmation. Hide anything personal.

title: Find 3 Opportunities Worth Applying To
short: Look up jobs, internships, scholarships, or summer programs and write down three to apply to, with any deadlines.
proof: Your list of three.

title: Improve One Part of Your Portfolio
short: Fix one thing in your portfolio, like a blurry photo of your work, an unclear description, or a broken link.
proof: The improved part. Hide anything personal.

title: Practice 5 Interview Questions
short: Write answers to five interview questions, like why you want the job or a time you solved a problem, and say them aloud.
proof: Your notes on the five answers.

title: Spend 30 Minutes Practicing a Job Skill
short: Practice something most jobs ask for, like typing, making a spreadsheet, or writing a clear, polite email.
proof: What you practiced, after the timer.

title: Add Something New to Your Resume or Portfolio
short: Add one thing that isn't listed yet, like a club role, an award, a summer job, or something you made.
proof: The new entry. Hide anything personal.

title: Research 3 Skills Required for a Job You Want
short: Look up postings for a job you want someday, like nurse or game designer, and write three skills they ask for.
proof: Your notes on the three skills.

title: Practice Explaining Something You Made
short: Pick something you made, like a science fair project or a video, and write what it was, what you did, and how it went.
proof: Your outline or notes.

title: Complete One Part of an Application
short: Finish one section of a job, school, or scholarship application, like the short essay or the activities list.
proof: The part you finished. Hide anything personal.

title: Work on Your Project for 30 Minutes
short: Do the next real step, like writing code, designing a shirt, editing your next video, or recording a song.
proof: What you worked on, after the timer.

title: Finish One Small Part of Your Project
short: Get one small piece fully done, like one app screen, one product photo, the chorus of a song, or a video intro.
proof: The finished part.

title: Make One Post or Video for Your Project
short: Make one finished post you could share, like a clip of your process, a product photo with a caption, or a song preview.
proof: The finished post or video.
template: Make One Post or Video for {project}

title: Improve One Page, Photo, or Screen
short: Redo one thing people see first, like a product photo, a video thumbnail, your site's home page, or an app screen.
proof: Before and after.

title: Fix One Thing Wrong With Your Project
short: Find one thing that's broken or off, like a bug, a dead link, a loose seam, or audio that's too quiet, and fix it.
proof: The fixed result.

title: Plan the Next 3 Steps for Your Project
short: Write three steps you can each do in one sitting, like sketching a logo, filming an intro, or fixing a sign-up page.
proof: Your written list of three.

title: Sketch One New Design
short: Sketch one new idea on paper or on a screen, like a shirt graphic, a logo, an app layout, or cover art for a song.
proof: What you made.

title: Check Your Views or Sales and Pick One Change
short: Look at one number, like video views, shop sales, or app downloads, and write one thing you'll change because of it.
proof: Your written decision. No customer or financial details.

title: Publish Something You Made
short: Finish and post one thing that's been sitting in drafts, like a video, a song, a shop item, or a blog post.
proof: What you published.

title: Improve Something You Made Yesterday
short: Open yesterday's work and make one clear change, like trimming a slow clip, fixing a design's colors, or tidying code.
proof: Before and after.

title: Turn One Idea Into a First Draft
short: Write or record a rough first version of one idea, like a video script, a song demo, or a product description.
proof: Your first draft.

title: Practice Your Skill for 30 Minutes
short: Practice by doing, not watching, like playing scales, speaking Spanish aloud, sketching, or solving a coding exercise.
proof: What you practiced, after the timer.

title: Complete One Lesson, Then Use What You Learned
short: Finish one lesson in a book, course, or app, then use it right away, like writing Spanish sentences with the new words.
proof: What you made with what you learned.

title: Practice What Trips You Up for 20 Minutes
short: Slowly repeat the one thing you keep getting wrong, like a chord change, Spanish verb endings, or drawing hands.
proof: What you practiced, after the timer.

title: Make One Small Thing Using Your Skill
short: Make one small, finished thing, like a one-page website, a short comic, a simple song, or a paragraph in Spanish.
proof: What you made.

title: Explain One Thing You Learned From Memory
short: Close the book or video and write out one thing you learned, like how a chord is built or a Spanish grammar rule.
proof: Your explanation, written from memory.

title: Create Something Worth Showing Someone
short: Make one finished piece you'd show a friend, like a full drawing, a recorded cover song, or a one-minute video.
proof: The finished piece.

title: Improve Something You Created Before
short: Open something you made weeks or months ago, like an old drawing, song, or essay, and redo one part better.
proof: Before and after.

title: Watch One Tutorial and Apply One Thing From It
short: Watch one how-to video, like a guitar lesson or a video-editing tip, then try that one thing yourself right away.
proof: What you made with it.

title: Recreate Something Without Following the Tutorial
short: Make something you learned from a video again with the video closed, like a drawing, a guitar riff, or a small program.
proof: What you recreated.

title: Clear Your Desk
short: Throw out trash, put away papers and chargers, and leave only what you need on your desk.
proof: Before and after of the desk.

title: Clean Up Your Room
short: Spend 15 minutes putting clothes away, clearing the floor, and making your bed.
proof: Before and after of the room.

title: Pack Everything You Need for Tomorrow
short: Pack your bag tonight with what you need tomorrow, like homework, your charger, and clothes for practice.
proof: What you packed.

title: Reset Your Workspace for Tomorrow
short: Put things back where they go and set out what you'll start with tomorrow, like the notebook you need first.
proof: Your workspace, ready.

title: Review Your Calendar for the Next 7 Days
short: Look at the next seven days and write down what's coming, like tests, practices, work shifts, and birthdays.
proof: Your written summary. No calendar screenshot needed.
